prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1400; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver regarding a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle entered the intersection on a red signal and struck the driver's door. Police report requested and reference number logged. Vehicle is drivable but has significant damage to the driver side. Tow was not required.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. Claimant reports neck and back strain after the impact and has started seeing a primary care provider. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and states they are handling the matter directly. Claimant provided photos of the vehicle damage and the intersection. Medical authorization form sent to the claimant for signature.

Entry 3: Spoke with the at-fault driver's carrier. Liability is disputed in part, with the other driver stating their light was yellow when they entered. Requested signal timing data from the municipality and reviewed the scene photos submitted by both parties. Witness contact information obtained from the police report is being followed up.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspected at the repair facility. Estimate written for body repair on the driver door, rear quarter panel, and side sill. Supplemental damage noted on the wheel assembly and a sensor bracket. Repair estimate sent to the claimant and the claimant has been advised of their right to choose the repair shop. Rental vehicle coverage confirmed under the policy.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with the claimant to check on injury progress. Claimant reports stiffness and ongoing discomfort but no emergency treatment. Claimant was reminded that medical records and bills should be forwarded as they are received. File remains open pending medical documentation, the liability determination, and repair completion. Diary set for further review.
